paragraphs: The day's rhythm is zone setup, work, and closeout. Place cones and signs and preserve a buffer before patching with cold material or hot asphalt and sealing cracks by machine. On nonwork days, patrol for potholes, water damage, and guardrail problems and schedule repairs. Winter is hardest: snowplows operate overnight in shifts, followed by surface checks and additional deicer.

U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) data show about 159,100 maintenance workers employed in 2024, projected to reach 163,900 by 2034. That is a net increase of about 4,800 jobs, with roughly 12,300 annual openings. Median annual pay is about $49,100 in 2026 (BLS OOH, 2026).

paragraphs: A 3/10 score places highway maintenance in a relatively low AI exposure infrastructure role. People perform patching, obstruction clearance, and snow removal on site, while AI handles only peripheral inspection, records, and scheduling. Core work cannot soon be replaced.

Low exposure is no reason for complacency. Drone inspections already reduce manual defect-finding. Learn inspection equipment and advance toward mechanized maintenance crews and project management, turning physical work into technical work for greater stability.

Young entrants should prepare for outdoor shifts and constant weather exposure. A special-equipment route can include loader and snowplow credentials, which increase competitiveness for mechanized maintenance.

Advance toward mechanized maintenance and technical management. Learn inspection vehicles and drones, earn equipment credentials, and use inspection and repair data to progress from manual worker to maintenance planner.

People with construction or equipment-operation experience can transition by learning maintenance processes and safety standards, especially work-zone habits. Emphasize equipment operation, procedural discipline, and night-shift availability in interviews.

Maintenance teams struggle to recruit. Equipment training, winter allowances, and rotating rest can improve retention. Drones and inspection vehicles should reduce ineffective patrols and concentrate workers on repairs and emergencies.
